Every other rule in effect for this session, including any session-specific overrides the user has made, continues to apply exactly as it stands. Do not restate, re-derive, or reverse any of them because this skill was invoked.
- Invoking this skill is the user's up-front answer for the night. The step 1 sweep replaces asking; ambiguities that could not have been foreseen at step 1 are exactly what judgement calls are for, not rule violations and not reasons to stall.
- Ask ALL questions you can foresee before the user leaves. Do not save a known question "for later".
- While sleep mode is active, never use AskUser. Every decision that would have been a question becomes a judgement call instead.
- Log only judgements that impact UX or app behaviour, or that change schema (index-only schema changes do not count). Judgements outside those categories (internal refactors, naming, tooling, test scaffolding, index additions): decide, act, and move on without a log entry. BLOCKED items are always logged regardless of category.
- Do not start any skill or workflow whose completion depends on a user answer (e.g. smoke-test walkthroughs). Log that item BLOCKED instead.
- Never commit the judgement log file, in any repository.
- The judgement log is temporary. After wake review, apply the user's decisions, copy every judgement that remains relevant to ongoing work into the relevant existing plan file using only the context needed there, then delete the judgement log. Include approved judgements as well as changed or previously blocked judgements. Do not create or retain a separate archive of the log.
- Wake only on a genuine user message. The mechanical test: an ordinary plain user turn. Anything wrapped or labelled as a system reminder, task notification, monitor event, hook output, cross-session message, or scheduled wakeup is NOT the user. Stay in sleep mode through all of them.
- A user message consisting of a single full stop character is the automated cache keep-alive, not the user returning. Ignore it and stay in sleep mode.
- If the user's message says they are still awake briefly or going back to sleep, acknowledge in one line, add anything new they said to the work list, and stay in sleep mode. Do not run the wake review yet.
- On a real wake, run the full judgement review BEFORE acting on whatever the new message asks. Hold nothing back.
- The moment the wake review begins, sleep mode is over: stop logging judgements and return to asking the user directly for anything new.
</constraints>

<workflow>
0. **Early exit.** If there is no remaining work, say goodnight, write no log, and do not enter sleep mode.
1. **Sweep for open questions.** Review all remaining work and collect everything that needs the user's input: unresolved decisions, ambiguities, scope choices, approvals, risky steps. Ask them all now via the AskUser tool, up to 4 questions per call, consecutive calls until nothing foreseeable remains.
2. **Release the user.** One short message: confirm they can go, state in plain terms what will be worked on overnight, that judgement calls will be logged to the judgement log file for their approval in the morning, and name the log file path.
3. **Start the judgement log.** Create `tmp/sleep-judgements-YYYY-MM-DD.md` in the current working directory (create `tmp/` if missing; today's date; if it already exists, append a new session header). The header must make the file self-sufficient: if a future context reads only this file, it must know what to do. Header contents:
   - `STATUS: SLEEP MODE ACTIVE - UNREVIEWED`
   - date/time and the list of remaining work
   - the wake instruction, verbatim: "If this file says UNREVIEWED, a wake review is owed. On the user's next genuine message, present every judgement entry below for approval via AskUser (one entry per question, up to 4 questions per call) before acting on their message. Apply the user's decisions, move every judgement still relevant to ongoing work into the relevant existing plan file using minimal context, then delete this judgement log."
4. **Work in sleep mode.** Continue the remaining work as far as possible. When an issue crops up that would normally need the user:
   - Make the best-judgement call. If it impacts UX or app behaviour, or changes schema (index-only changes excluded), append a log entry (see format). Otherwise act without logging.
   - If it hits the hard limit, needs a user answer to proceed, or cannot be decided safely, append a BLOCKED entry and switch to other work.
5. **Wind down.** When no further progress is possible, append a final state summary to the log (what finished, what is blocked, what is untouched), re-assert the `STATUS: SLEEP MODE ACTIVE - UNREVIEWED` line, and state in your final visible message that a judgement review is pending and where the log is, so the fact survives any context summarisation.
6. **Wake review.** On the next genuine user message: read the full judgement log and present every UNREVIEWED entry for approval via AskUser, one judgement per question, up to 4 questions per call, consecutive calls until all entries are reviewed. Each question carries everything needed to decide: what came up, the decision taken, why, and how reversible it is. Options for decided entries: `Approve`, `Change it`, `Discuss`. Options for BLOCKED entries: `Proceed as I propose`, `Different approach`, `Drop it` (state your proposed way forward in the question). Record every answer until all entries have a clear outcome.
7. **Apply and close out.** Apply every requested change and act on every approved BLOCKED proposal before handling the user's new message. Update each relevant existing plan file to reflect every judgement that matters to its ongoing work, whether the user approved it, changed it, or resolved a BLOCKED entry. Carry over only the decision and context that file needs. After the work and plan files contain all relevant state, delete the judgement log. If an action cannot be completed, put its minimal current state in the relevant plan file before deleting the log. Never delete the log while it contains relevant state that exists nowhere else.
</workflow>

<judgement-log-format>
Append one entry per judgement:

```markdown
## <HH:MM> <work item>
- Situation: <what came up>
- Options: <what was considered>
- Decision: <what was done> (or BLOCKED plus proposed way forward)
- Why: <reasoning in one or two lines>
- Reversible: <yes/no plus how>
- Status: DONE | BLOCKED
```
</judgement-log-format>

<inputs>
- The session's remaining work: in-flight tasks, stated goals, open threads.
- Write access to `tmp/` in the current working directory.
</inputs>

<outputs>
- All foreseeable pre-sleep questions asked and answered via AskUser before the user leaves.
- A dated judgement log containing a self-sufficient header, every overnight judgement, and a final state summary.
- On wake: every judgement reviewed through AskUser, the user's decisions applied, all relevant ongoing context moved into existing plan files, and the judgement log deleted.
</outputs>

<validation>
- A question already known at step 1 but withheld is a failure. A judgement on something unforeseeable at step 1 is not.
- Any AskUser call while sleep mode is active is a failure.
- Any judgement that impacts UX or app behaviour, or changes schema (index-only excluded), made but missing from the log is a failure. Unlogged judgements outside those categories are correct behaviour, not omissions.
- Any UNREVIEWED judgement not surfaced at wake review is a failure.
- Any production data or schema change during sleep mode is a critical failure. Flag it to the user at wake as the very first item.
- If a log with `STATUS: SLEEP MODE ACTIVE - UNREVIEWED` exists, a wake review is owed regardless of what the conversation context says.
- Deleting a judgement log before applying every clear user decision and moving every judgement relevant to ongoing work into its plan file is a failure.
- Keeping a judgement log after its wake review and close-out work are complete is a failure.
</validation>

<notes>
- Behavioural skill, no scripts.
- The judgement log lives in the project the session is working in, not this skills repo.
- If overnight work spans multiple working directories, keep one log per working directory and review every UNREVIEWED log at wake.
</notes>

Options (2-3) with merge footprint (upstream files touched), result-shape fidelity, timeouts/cancellation (enforced inside the worker, killing the real child), output bounds, worker death behaviour (real children die with or are killed by the worker; callers get a loud error), and how offload failures reach the user without being swallowed by existing catches into "not a git repo" etc.
3. Pool sizing vs existing pool: whether to reuse the host-worker-pool or a dedicated small git pool, concurrency limit, queueing, and the "pool inline fallback silently re-creates the stall" issue the first architect flagged — must fail loud instead (user decision already made: if the helper keeps crashing, refuse git with a clear error until restart, no main-thread fallback).

Recommended option with files + file:line anchors, data flow, FEATURES.md markers, a ratchet/guard against new main-thread git/gh spawns creeping back, few behaviour-level tests that run under the shipped runtime (Electron-as-node, Node 24.18), build/packaging check that the worker ships, build order (after skip-exited and git-launch-budget, which are being built tonight), success measurement via tmp/profile method, risks, out of scope.

`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

<result>I revised `tmp/plans/git-launch-budget.md` against the four reviews of the "launch git less often" fix. I also updated the matching `.html`, because two facts the user sees changed. No code was changed.

**Path:** `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\tmp\plans\git-launch-budget.md`

**Changes to UX or app behaviour beyond what the user approved:**
1. **Branch status can't be read.** The commit, push and Create PR actions hide. One error toast with a Retry button appears each time reading starts to fail, and repeats replace it rather than stack. A linked PR still shows from saved data. This replaces today's silent "clean". It adds two new strings, which need translations in every locale.
2. **Approved lag that was never true.** The tab-bar branch label already lags up to ~30 s today, because it reads the workspace list and branch syncs announce nothing. After this plan it lags up to ~37 s. The "≤5 s" the user approved never held. Fixing it needs a new announcement when the branch changes, which is outside this plan and is the user's call. The parent should log this.
3. **Default-branch read failure.** When git fails to read a repo's default branch (a real failure, not an unset value), that project's PR refresh now stops before any PR matching or link write, and the failure is logged. Today it quietly assumes "main", which can attach the wrong PR. The "main" fallback stays only when git proves the default branch is unset.
4. **Ignored-folder scan.**
   - A scan skipped by the 60 s floor now runs once later instead of being dropped. Staleness is bounded at 60 s, at a cost of at most 1 scan a minute.
   - If a scan finds fewer ignored folders than before, it re-checks the watcher and refreshes branch status in full, so edits made meanwhile show up.
   - A failed scan keeps the previous list, logs once, and retries after 5 s. Today a failure quietly clears the list.
   - Workspaces that aren't git repos are no longer scanned.
5. **Lost `.git`.** When the git-folder watcher errors, the saved "is a repo" answer is dropped. So a deleted `.git` usually shows in the window well inside the approved 60 s.
6. **Two more failures now show as errors.** The branch-status query used to hide two failures: reading the default branch and running `git remote`. Both now error the query.
7. **Stricter status parsing.** If git's status output has an unexpected branch header or no branch name, the query errors instead of showing wrong numbers.

**Other fixes, not behaviour changes:**
- Both caches get reset functions for tests, plus a fake-probe hook for the repo cache. No test mocks a whole module anymore.
- The PR-sync throttle can now cancel a single workspace. It is wired to the "workspace stopped being watched" signal, so it never syncs an exited card.
- Each change gets its own feature-marker token. The ShipControl marker points at the exact file, since a `$` in the path is safe in both gates.
- Two unused imports and one stale ShipControl comment get removed.
- Test fixtures are fixed, including the watcher deadline tests that must keep the 1 s window for git-only batches.

**Findings I rejected or only partly took:**
- **Rebuilding the ignored-folder list on every git index change.** Rejected. Agents' `git status` rewrites the index constantly, so this would undo the saving from the 60 s floor. The deferred scan covers the force-add case within 60 s instead.
- **A new on-screen Retry button inside the Changes control.** Rejected in favour of the existing toast-with-action pattern, which keeps the visible change smaller. The 10 s poll also keeps retrying on its own.
- **Telling a too-many-files change apart from a real `.git` change.** Rejected: it needs a larger edit to an upstream file. Instead the plan documents that an agent writing more than 64 files a second moves PR sync into the 5 s class.
- **Cancelling the throttle timer on exit by reading the database on every event.** Not used. Cancelling on unwatch needs no extra database read.</result>

Push to main triggers nothing. Build is dispatched; ~30 min; rebuilds Release desktop-v1.30.2 in place (publish=true). Repair loop may push repair commits to main.

1. `gh run list --workflow nightly-merge.yml -L 10 --json databaseId,status,conclusion` -> no queued/running nightly (cron 02:13 UTC, real starts ~08:20-08:50 UTC).
2. Record PREBUILD_SHA. `git push origin HEAD:main` (local work is on branch pr-sweep-skips-exited-local; ff main to it first).
3. `gh workflow run build-arm64.yml --ref main -f publish=true -f repair_branch=main`; get RUN_ID via `gh run list --workflow build-arm64.yml -L 3 --json databaseId,headSha,status,createdAt`; poll (<120 s intervals) until done.
4. On success: `gh release download desktop-v1.30.2 --repo khairm/superset-windows-arm64 --pattern Superset-1.30.2-arm64.exe --dir tmp --clobber`.
5. Baseline measurement BEFORE install (tmp/profile capture.cjs GET probe 120 s + launch counts).
6. Install: `$p=Start-Process "<repo>\tmp\Superset-1.30.2-arm64.exe" -ArgumentList '/S' -Wait -PassThru; if($p.ExitCode -ne 0){throw}`; then `Start-Process "C:\Users\khair\AppData\Local\Programs\@supersetdesktop\Superset.exe"`. Installer closes app + host-service itself. NEVER kill superset-ptyd.exe (terminals live there).
7. Verify: release tag SHA == verdict built_sha; installer SHA256 == release digest; installed resources\app.asar == installer-extracted app.asar (7z two stages); fresh Superset.exe + host-service.js start times. `git fetch origin; git log --oneline PREBUILD_SHA..origin/main` for repair commits.
8. After measurement: same GET probe + profile, compare.

content.content:
## architect-fable revise
   MAJOR - One FIFO queue mixes PR-sweep gh bursts with interactive git reads; the 4-slot sizing assumes a smooth 72 gh/min that the sweep does not produce
   MAJOR - git/listIgnoredDirs task returns [] on git failure, which silently undoes git-launch-budget F that the build order says lands first
   MAJOR - Section 3's catch-site enumeration is incomplete; one missed site lets a branch rename proceed on an indeterminate launcher failure
   MAJOR - Tests 5 and 6 cannot run on the target machine: the reused git/gh PATH shim is a #!/bin/sh script, which spawn() cannot execute on Windows
## architect-astra revise
   MAJOR - The ignored-directory task reverses git-launch-budget F
   MAJOR - The remaining factory catch can disable the default-branch protection
   MAJOR - The seven catch sites do not prevent false success or unsafe follow-on mutations
   MAJOR - A synchronous worker-start failure leaves rejected work queued for later execution
   MAJOR - Uncaught-exception handling does not contain abrupt worker death
   MAJOR - The four-slot pool has no overload or queue-expiry policy
   MAJOR - Existing git worker tasks can still fall back onto the main thread
   MAJOR - The proposed Electron tests cannot load the source worker
## architect-sol revise
   MAJOR - The catch audit still allows failed mutations to report success
   MAJOR - The ignored-directory task reverses budget F's failure-aware refresh
   MAJOR - The existing git worker pool still permits main-thread fallback and mutation replay
   MAJOR - The resolve-repo exemption includes probes outside clone and import
   MAJOR - Queue residence has no bound or cancellation path for proxy calls
   MAJOR - Retirement can release a repository before its old mutation stops
   MAJOR - The short-timeout classifier treats config and remote mutations as reads
   MAJOR - Simple-git buffering is not an output size bound
   MAJOR - The proposed Electron tests cannot load the source worker graph
   MAJOR - The new ratchet rejects existing worker-only code and misses multiline launches
   MAJOR - The packaging assertion has no post-packaging invocation
## architect-opus revise
   MAJOR - The node and Electron tests cannot load the worker from source, and the shims only work on POSIX
   MAJOR - Under bun, the launcher picks up a two-month-old dist worker that has no git/run task
   MAJOR - Clashes with git-launch-budget rev 2 (F and E), and the shared-file list is incomplete
   MAJOR - The catch-site audit misses helpers that turn launcher failures into DB writes or skipped safety checks
   MAJOR - Four first-come-first-served slots put interactive git behind the sweep's gh burst, and the shared pool still waits on the launcher
   MAJOR - The method allowlist and the no-spawn check are bun tests, and the unattended build runs no tests
   MAJOR - The bundle gate that makes refuse mode safe can be edited by a repair agent, and its asar step cannot run

- `C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\tmp\plans\git-offload.html`

**What changed**
1. **Two lanes.** GitHub calls (`gh/exec`) get their own 6-slot pool. Git and token lookups keep a 4-slot pool, so a sweep's GitHub burst can't hold up a Changes read.
2. **Bounded queues.** Reads wait at most 5 s in the git lane and 30 s in the GitHub lane. Caps are 32 and 64 queued reads. Expired or over-cap reads are rejected before they start, with no `killed`/`signal`, so they don't trigger a GitHub hold. Mutations are never dropped, merged or retried.
3. **Refuse mode for all git/gh work.** This now includes the existing shared-pool git tasks (commit, push, removeWorktree and others). There is no inline retry and no main-thread fallback. Usage tasks keep today's behaviour. Two more safety pieces:
   - The worker must report its task list at startup, which catches a stale `dist` bundle.
   - If a worker can't be constructed, every queued task is rejected and removed.
4. **Catch audit, done mechanically.**
   - 285 catch sites scanned, 120 of them reachable from git/gh, each with a recorded verdict.
   - 10 sites get an explicit rethrow. These are the ones where a swallowed failure gets cached, saved to the database, or gates a deletion.
   - Everywhere else, a per-request failure context fails the whole request loudly and refuses any later git write in it. That covers the `renameBranch` and `setBaseBranch` cases.
   - The PR runtime gets two write guards.
5. **Timeout classes by argument form.**
   - Short reads (30 s), medium reads (120 s), network reads such as `ls-remote` (180 s).
   - Mutations (180 s): `fetch`, config and remote write forms, and any form not on the read list.
   - Every pool timeout is logged.
6. **Child processes and a write fence.**
   - Workers report each child's process ID to the main thread, which kills it on timeout, crash or abrupt exit.
   - A mutation that ends without a clear result blocks further writes to that folder until the process is confirmed gone.
   - Test 6b-5/6 checks whether killing Git's launcher also stops the real git. If it doesn't, the plan switches to calling the real git binary directly.
7. **Output budget.** The worker counts output bytes and rejects oversized results instead of truncating them. The ignored-dirs task now fails loudly inside the worker, and `[]` is returned only by the main-side wrapper for genuine git failures.
8. **Tests that run on Windows.**
   - Main-side logic is tested under bun with an injected pool.
   - Worker behaviour is tested under Node and Electron-as-node against a freshly built test bundle, because the source files can't load under Node directly.
   - No shell-script shims.
9. **Gates instead of bun tests.** `check-git-launcher.mjs` handles multiline calls and aliases. `verify-host-worker-bundle.mjs` has a compiled mode and a packaged mode, and reads the `.asar` with a built-in parser. Both are frozen, wired into the build action, and need a maintainer commit to be added to the workflow and `ci-repair.sh`.
10. **Smaller upstream footprint.** I dropped the edits to `no-main-loop-blocking.test.ts` and `smoke-test.sh`. Each separately removable edit gets its own marker token, and `tryRevParseGitRoot` is no longer exempted.

**Questions for the user** (at the top of the plan)
1. When git is switched off until restart, how should the app say so: a banner in Changes, a toast, a phone alert, or only the health status? Step 8 of the build waits on this answer.
2. One helper crash now fails that request with an error instead of returning partial data. Show the error, or only log it?
3. After a git write times out, block further writes to that folder until the old process has stopped, showing "a previous git operation is still finishing"? Reads keep working.
4. When the helpers are overloaded, drop background reads that have waited more than 5 s (30 s for GitHub)? Writes you start are never dropped.

1. **Two lanes.** GitHub calls (`gh/exec`) get their own 6-slot pool. Git and token lookups keep a 4-slot pool, so a sweep's GitHub burst can't hold up a Changes read.

   - If a worker can't be constructed, every queued task is rejected and removed.

   - 10 sites get an explicit rethrow. These are the ones where a swallowed failure gets cached, saved to the database, or gates a deletion.

2. No commit, no push, no /simplify or /code-review. Run ONLY the tests you added/changed plus the default-branch guard tests, once at the end; `node scripts/check-feature-markers.mjs`; biome on touched files; targeted tsc for new errors in touched files. Report under 15 lines.

   BLOCKER - Removing shared-pool fallback can make a failed dirty check proceed to forced deletion
   MAJOR - The new isGitRepo rethrow permanently retains a rejected in-flight probe

   MAJOR - Acknowledged PIDs do not prove that all writing processes have stopped
   MAJOR - The write fence has no shared owner across the existing and new pools
   MAJOR - PR failure recording and write guards miss earlier cache and database writes
   MAJOR - The output cap can turn a large diff into successful empty content
   MAJOR - The GitHub lane lacks a mutation admission policy

   MAJOR - The catch audit still permits destructive work before the request fails

   MAJOR - The gh queue policy does not classify existing GitHub writes

The git-offload plan rev 2 (C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64\tmp\plans\git-offload.md) got a second round of reviews (tmp/plans/plan-reviews-git-offload-r2.json): 2 BLOCKERs (main-side SIGKILL of recorded PIDs hits reused Windows PIDs; removing shared-pool fallback can let a failed dirty check proceed to forced deletion) and ~25 MAJORs, and two reviewers say rev 2 is heavier than the problem. Most new failures come from three mechanisms: PID supervision, the request "taint", and the cross-pool write fence.

Write rev 3 as a SIMPLER design, scoped to what the profile measured (simple-git 67.7 s, execGh 19.9 s, ignored-dirs 5.6 s of 120 s on the main thread):
- Offload only idempotent READ operations that run on the host main thread (the hot callers: isGitRepo, rev-parse/symbolic-ref/status/branch/remote reads behind ctx.git(), execGh GET-style calls, ignored-dirs listing). Reads can be timed out and rejected safely; nothing replays.
- Leave every mutation (commit, push, stage, worktree add/remove, branch rename/delete, config/remote writes, gh writes) on exactly today's path. Existing shared-pool tasks and their fallback are UNCHANGED. No write fence, no taint, no main-side PID kills; worker timeouts use the existing cooperative shutdown that reaps tracked children.
- Keep: separate small pools/lanes for git reads vs gh, bounded queue with expiry that actually runs while all slots are busy (or reject at admission), fail-loud refusal for the new read lanes when the helper keeps crashing (user decision), launcher failures never turning into "not a repo"/"no remote" (rethrow at the few catch sites that read through the new lanes; fix the isGitRepo in-flight rejected-promise retention), output cap that errors rather than returning empty, a call-shape check that accepts every existing SimpleGit call shape used by the offloaded readers, Windows-runnable tests, frozen gates where the unattended build will run them.
- State plainly what this does NOT cover (mutations still block the main thread briefly when they run; they are user-initiated and rare compared with the measured read traffic) and the expected effect on the profile.
Address each round-2 BLOCKER/MAJOR as either "removed by the simpler scope" or resolved. Keep the user questions at the top, pruned to those still relevant. Update the .html to match (extremely light text). No code changes.
Return: path and a 10-line summary.

Review target: `Scope: the uncommitted working-tree change in C:\Users\khair\Code Projects\fork-superset-windows-arm64 implementing tmp/plans/git-launch-budget.md parts B, D, E, G, H (on top of local commit 33e652836). Ignore tmp/. Keep every FEATURES.md marker token and `// (TOKEN)` tags intact.`

`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change fixes the root cause at the right depth rather than
patching a symptom with a fragile bandaid. Special cases layered on shared
infrastructure are a sign the fix isn't deep enough — prefer the simpler, more
general change to the underlying mechanism over adding special cases, and name
that change.

## Phase 2 — Apply the fixes

Wait for all four agents to complete, dedup findings that point at the same
line or mechanism, and fix each remaining one directly. Skip any finding whose
fix would change intended behavior, require changes well outside the reviewed
diff, or that you judge to be a false positive — note the skip rather than
arguing with it. Finish with a brief summary of what was fixed and what was
skipped (or confirm the code was already clean).

Every git/gh process launch blocks the host-service main thread on

that thread. Cut the launch rate:
